summary: Burst 502/503s from GPU worker thread starvation during large-embedding job with keepalive churn
description:
Issue summary:
Customers observe short bursts (~30s-2m) of 502/503 responses originating at the API gateway when a large embedding job (approx 1.2M tokens across many small requests) runs concurrently with normal traffic. Rate of errors correlates with embedding job spikes and periods of many short-lived streaming sessions (keepalive churn).

Impact:
- LuminaSearch (dedicated) reported 15-30% request error-rate increase during bursts, impacting live search indexing.
- Errors are transient but repeatable with similar workload pattern; downstream retries amplify load.

Environment:
- Prod, us-east, Dedicated GPU pool (A100s), serving-runtime v2026.02.7, nvml driver v470.x, API gateway v1.14.3

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Start large embedding job: 12k concurrent small embedding requests batched by customer SDK into many parallel connections.
2) Introduce a stream of short-lived streaming sessions to simulate keepalive churn (many short connections).
3) Observe API gateway 502/503 spikes and increased watchdog restarts on runtime.

Observed logs / metrics:
- api-gateway logs show upstream reset / 502 with code "upstream connection closed" during bursts.
- serving-runtime logs contain repeated lines: "watchdog: gpu-worker-thread timeout, resetting worker pid=***" and occasional "nvml timeout waiting for response (2000ms)".
- GPU utilization shows high but not fully saturated. CPU on runtime host shows high runnable thread count in process responsible for driver IO.
- KV-cache eviction rate spikes, prefetch queue length increases.

Notes on customer session:
- Customer reported increased retrying logic in their client; they attempted backoff which reduced but did not eliminate the bursts.
- No config changes on customer side during incident window.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: driver-level stalls (nvml) or GPU-thread pool contention causing runtime watchdog to reset GPU worker threads. This triggers inflight requests to be aborted and returns 502/503 at api-gateway.

What we checked so far:
- Correlated timestamped runtime watchdog logs with api-gateway 502 windows; near 95th percentile alignment.
- Examined NVML kernel messages and dmesg for driver resets: found repeated nvml timeouts (2000ms) during bursts but no full GPU reset.
- Traced runtime worker thread stacks (coredump/stacktrace sampling) — many threads blocked on driver ioctl or on futexes in the IO path.
- Prefetch subsystem shows long queue growth and KV-cache lock contention, likely increasing number of small GPU requests and locking driver IO.
- API gateway healthchecks show upstream connection closures when worker pids are being restarted by watchdog.

Hypothesis refinement:
- Combination of (1) high-volume small embedding requests causing a large number of short driver IO ops and (2) keepalive churn preventing connection reuse leads to GPU worker threads spending disproportionate time on small serial IO, increasing latency per-op and tripping watchdog thresholds.
- Result: worker reset -> inflight abort -> api-gateway 502/503 waves.

Immediate mitigations tested in staging:
- Increase runtime watchdog timeout from 1.5s to 3s on a canary; reduced observed resets under same synthetic load (but increases time to detect real GPU deadlocks).
- Enabled coalescing of extremely small embedding ops into micro-batches on canary pathway; significantly lowered driver IO ops/sec and avoided watchdog trips in tests.
- Toggled connection keepalive reuse configuration in api-gateway (longer keepalive) to reduce churn; tests showed improved connection reuse and fewer 502s.
comments: Priya Sharma (2026-03-12): Customer LuminaSearch reported spikes at 09:10-09:30 UTC; provided request sampling and s3 logs. Escalating to infra oncall.
Ethan Park (2026-03-12): Reproduced in internal staging with synthetic workload; saw watchdog resets in runtime. Opening this ticket for cross-team coordination.

SRE Team (2026-03-13): Observed nvml timeouts in node logs for 3 hosts in the dedicated pool. Stack samples show driver ioctl bottleneck. Suggested temporary scaling down of concurrent embedding shards for customer.
Infra Eng (2026-03-13): Deployed runtime canary with increased watchdog and micro-batching patch to 5% of traffic; initial telemetry looks promising (no resets under same load).
Support (2026-03-14): Communicated temporary mitigation (requesting customer to throttle concurrent embedding shards by 40%) — customer accepted while we prepare broader fix.
action_items: Deploy micro-batching feature to dedicated pool behind config flag (owner: Runtime Team)
Evaluate default watchdog timeout and make adaptive threshold based on per-tenant request size distribution (owner: Runtime Team)
Add driver-level instrumentation to correlate nvml latency per-op (owner: Infra)
Document recommended client-side concurrency limits for large-embedding jobs and add to onboarding docs (owner: DevEx)
Schedule postmortem and include customer impact summary and timeline (owner: Support)
resolution: In progress - temporary customer throttle applied while runtime micro-batching is rolled out canary->prod. If canary metrics remain stable for 48h, we'll flip flag for affected dedicated pool and update docs. Final resolution to include monitoring for nvml-op-latency and adaptive watchdog heuristics.
